NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE III: DEFENSE, RAIDS AND THE FALLEN (LCC-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
"If anyone comes to raid our homeland, we'll be ready." Isola's people are peaceful but no pushovers: stamping dances and war chants, watch fires and plans, raids fended off or not, prisoners and bargains, and how the village honors those who defended it.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: The village needs more spearheads: use the sacred black stone from the old shrine, or search the far beach for ordinary stone.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: The warriors need more spearheads, and the best stone on the island is the black glassy stone around the old shrine, which some villagers hold sacred. (subject) says the village's safety matters more than old stones. (friend) says some things are not for taking, and there is ordinary flint on the far beach. What should they do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) takes the stone, with a quiet apology spoken over it. The spearheads are the sharpest the village has ever made. Some villagers will not touch them. Some villagers will not speak to (subject). The warriors are glad of them.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) and a team walk to the far beach and spend three days gathering and knapping ordinary flint. The spearheads are good enough. The shrine stays as it is. (subject) admits, privately, that (subject.he/she) was relieved not to be the one to take it.
